subject: Acme renewal & expansion — recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Young <michael.young@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-23T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Acme renewal & expansion — recap and next steps

Thanks Michael — great call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of where Acme is today
- Current usage: ~75M tokens/month for ingestion + generation across search and chat workloads.
- Peak latency requirements: 250ms P95 for customer-facing chat.
- Pain points: occasional latency spikes during batch exports, cost variability during heavy training-run replays, and lack of predictable reserved capacity for marketing spikes.

Goals discussed
- Lock in predictable unit cost and guaranteed capacity for Q4 holiday surge.
- Add an embeddings-heavy reranking workload for product search (estimated +30% token volume).
- Maintain current response quality, prefer Redwood-managed quantization recommendations rather than building custom infra.

Proposed expansion path (high level)
1) Renewal (12 mo) for base usage with dedicated pool sizing to cover 1.2x current baseline.
2) Add dedicated burst capacity for Q4 (reserve in Dedicated with optional burst credits).
3) Pilot reranking workload on a small shard (1–2 models) in August, review perf/quality in September, expand in October.

Deliverables I will send by EOD
- Usage report (attached) showing token trends and P95 latencies.
- Draft amendment with proposed reserved capacity and pricing (attached).

Immediate asks for Acme
- Confirm procurement contact and timing for contract review.
- Confirm internal owners for the reranking pilot (engineering contact + QA owner).
- Agree on a short technical check-in next week to validate latency targets on dedicated pool.

Next meetings
- Proposed: 30-min technical sync w/ engineering on Jul 29 or Jul 30.

Attachments: [Attachment: 20260723-usage-report.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)], [Attachment: acme-amendment-v2.docx (Docx, 85KB)]

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with the amendment and HubSpot link for the deal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
From: Michael Young <michael.young@acme.com>

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa — this matches our understanding. A few quick clarifications: 

- The reranking workload will be owned by Priya (search engineering) and QA will be led by Sam. I looped them internally; I can introduce them to your team once we have a proposed pilot scope.
- For the Q4 burst: what does billing look like for burst credits vs reserved capacity? We need predictability — procurement will push back if there are too many variable line items.
- Timeline: procurement review typically takes 2–3 weeks once we have a redline-ready amendment. Our renewal is effective 2026-10-01; ideally signed by mid-September.

Happy to meet Jul 29 for the technical check-in — 10am PT works for me.

On the amendment: can you include a standard SLA for latency and an explicit fallback model in case of capacity constraints? That would help expedite internal approval.

Thanks,
Michael
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
michael.young@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Young <michael.young@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-23T10:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme renewal & expansion — recap and next steps

Perfect — thanks Michael. Quick answers below and next steps.

Billing for burst vs reserved capacity
- Reserved capacity: monthly committed fee covering baseline throughput (predictable).
- Burst credits: priced separately but capped per month in the proposed amendment; we can set a soft cap and a clear overage rate to avoid surprise charges. I’ve reflected a capped-burst option in acme-amendment-v2.docx.

SLA and fallback model
- We will include a latency SLA (250ms P95 target) and a documented fallback policy that routes to a slightly lower-cost model variant when Dedicated pool is saturated. Fallback behavior and QoS priorities are explicitly called out in section 4 of the amendment.

Pilot scope
- Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot on a 10% shard of product search traffic, run against a re-ranking model (open model variant x-small), success criteria: <=5% quality delta vs current production, and P95 <= 300ms on dedicated pool.

Next steps
1) I’ll share HubSpot deal link and updated quote (sending now).
2) David — can you take point on procurement cadence and confirm if a PO or full SOW is preferred?
3) Michael — confirm Jul 29 10am PT for technical sync and I’ll send calendar invite.

Attachments: [Attachment: acme-amendment-v2.docx (Docx, 85KB)]

Marissa
